source_native_structure.latent_computational_state: Parallel capacity-limited WM and slower RL action-value states; final trial policy supplies action evidence to multiple accumulators.
source_native_structure.update_or_learning_rule: RL and WM prediction-error/value updates inherited from RLWM; WM is fast/capacity-limited and decays/interferes, while RL updates incrementally.
source_native_structure.decision_or_control_operator: Linear ballistic accumulation with collapsing bounds; accumulator rates are driven by the RL/WM policy and the decision bound is allowed to vary with set size as a proactive-control term.
model_variants: PADDL joint choice+RT model with collapsing LBA bounds
held-out test-phase prediction using RL values learned during training

operator_source_descriptions.INT-13:parallel-rlwm-update-mixture: Parallel RL and working-memory value updates form the source policy; WM provides rapid capacity-limited learning while RL is slower and incremental.
operator_source_descriptions.INT-13:lba-choice-rt-accumulation: The source augments RLWM with a linear ballistic accumulator so action values drive multiple response accumulators and both choice and reaction-time distributions are fit jointly.
operator_source_descriptions.INT-13:setsize-proactive-bound: The decision threshold is modeled as a function of set size, with collapsing-bound and fixed-bound alternatives used to test proactive response caution.

direct_ancestry_basis: The source states that modeling began from a recent RLWM model identified as Westbrook et al. 2025, DOI 10.1038/s41467-025-61099-0.
The source explicitly frames the joint RLWM/RT construction as extending prior McDougle & Collins work, DOI 10.3758/s13423-020-01774-z.

profiles.source_scope: Inherited exact PLOS raw PDF receipt, existing INT01×INT14 source-native audit, and current first-party HTML review of theoretical model, inference, planning, limits and S1 Appendix.

source_native_structure.latent_computational_state: A latent hierarchy H partitions low-level graph states into connected clusters with high-level graph nodes and bridge edges; graph topology, task distribution and rewards constrain the hierarchy.
source_native_structure.update_or_learning_rule: Bayesian inversion of a generative environment model; posterior P(H|D) is approximated with Metropolis-within-Gibbs MCMC, updating hierarchy components conditionally.
source_native_structure.decision_or_control_operator: The inferred hierarchy supports hierarchical planning with HBFS/shortest-path operations; different experiments use hierarchy-conditioned choices, expected reward, or posterior-entropy reduction.
model_variants: HBFS hierarchical planner versus flat BFS / alternative accounts

operator_source_descriptions.INT-14:connected-crp-graph-hierarchy: A CRP prior clusters graph states subject to a connected-cluster constraint, yielding a hierarchical graph with bridge structure rather than task-set/action-policy clusters.
operator_source_descriptions.INT-14:mcmc-hierarchy-posterior: The source estimates the posterior over latent hierarchies with Metropolis-within-Gibbs sampling because exact posterior inference is intractable.
operator_source_descriptions.INT-14:hierarchical-bfs-planning: The inferred hierarchy is used for hierarchical shortest-path planning with HBFS and for hierarchy-conditioned behavioral predictions.

supplements.role: S1 Appendix supplemental results, methods, and discussion

adverse_source_limits: Shared CRP with INT-01 is a constituent only; clustered object, posterior/update and planning target differ.
The paper does not establish global optimality of the whole generative model.
HBFS is used as a planning realization without a strong claim that it is the unique cognitively plausible planner.
Large-graph exact posterior inference is intractable and approximated by MCMC.
No direct ancestor DOI is promoted from thematic or experimental predecessor citations alone.

profiles.source_scope: Inherited PLOS raw PDF, prior bounded G1 P18 comparison, INT01 source-scoped comparison, and current first-party HTML review of MB/MF value computation, conflict-sensitive drift diffusion, variants and adverse limits.

source_native_structure.latent_computational_state: Parallel model-based and model-free action values plus between-system and within-system conflict quantities at two stages of the task.
source_native_structure.update_or_learning_rule: Standard two-step MB/MF reinforcement-learning values are estimated first; conflict measures derived from those values enter a second-stage diffusion fit.
source_native_structure.decision_or_control_operator: A drift-diffusion decision layer maps value terms and conflict regressors to drift, starting preference and boundary separation, allowing conflict effects on controller influence and decision caution to be separated.

operator_source_descriptions.INT-15:mb-mf-value-computation: Model-based and model-free reinforcement-learning values are computed for the two-step task and provide the value inputs and conflict quantities used by the decision layer.
operator_source_descriptions.INT-15:conflict-sensitive-ddm: A drift-diffusion model uses MB/MF value and conflict regressors to explain choices and reaction times, separating value influence from decision-process effects.
operator_source_descriptions.INT-15:boundary-caution-modulation: Decision boundary separation changes with value conflict, operationalizing a conflict-related change in response caution rather than a new value-learning rule.

correction_and_supplement_bundle.correction_status: NO_CORRECTION IDENTIFIED IN W6 FIRSTPARTY ARTICLE-PAGE REVIEW; NOT AN EXHAUSTIVE PUBLISHER CORRECTION INDEX CLAIM

supplements.role: S1 Text parameter estimates and auxiliary analyses

adverse_source_limits: Within-system and between-system conflict are substantially correlated, and the task does not empirically identify a unique exact conflict form.
The paper explicitly describes the combined DDM as a statistical approximation rather than a mechanistic account of the full cognitive decision process.
Generic MB/MF components and standard RL are inherited constituents, not evidence of a globally independent family.
Bounded difference from G1 P18 concerns tested operators only and does not certify genealogical independence.

profiles.source_scope: Inherited PLOS raw PDF, prior bounded G1 P09 comparison, and current first-party HTML review of AuGMEnT learning equations, attentional feedback tags, traces, RPE-gated plasticity, SARSA(lambda) correspondence and source limits.

source_native_structure.latent_computational_state: Association-network regular and memory units carry current and persistent task-relevant activity; synaptic traces/tags retain credit information across delayed response and reward events.
source_native_structure.update_or_learning_rule: Response-selection feedback converts local traces into tags; a globally broadcast reward-prediction-error/neuromodulatory signal changes tagged synapses. Tag decay is shown to correspond to SARSA(lambda) eligibility traces under a parameter mapping.
source_native_structure.decision_or_control_operator: The network selects responses and feeds the selected response back to earlier processing/memory layers, providing the attentional credit-assignment signal that creates or transforms tags.

operator_source_descriptions.INT-16:response-feedback-synaptic-tags: Selected responses send attentional feedback to earlier association/memory stages, turning locally maintained traces into synaptic tags for delayed credit assignment.
operator_source_descriptions.INT-16:neuromodulated-tagged-plasticity: A global reward-prediction-error neuromodulatory signal interacts with tagged synapses to determine plasticity while tag formation itself depends on local information.
operator_source_descriptions.INT-16:sarsa-lambda-tag-correspondence: The source derives a precise correspondence between AuGMEnT tag decay and SARSA(lambda) eligibility traces under alpha = 1 - lambda gamma.

correction_and_supplement_bundle.correction_status: NO CORRECTION OR PAPER-SPECIFIC SUPPORTING FILE IDENTIFIED IN W6 FIRSTPARTY ARTICLE-PAGE REVIEW; NOT AN EXHAUSTIVE PUBLISHER INDEX CLAIM

adverse_source_limits: The model does not specify a unique biological mechanism generating persistent activity; recurrent activity is one of several possible implementations discussed.
Synaptic tags correspond to eligibility traces and AuGMEnT maps to SARSA(lambda), so generic reinforcement-plasticity language cannot establish an independent family.
The source is a biologically plausible network simulation, not direct in-vivo confirmation of the proposed synapse-specific mechanism.
Generic neuromodulatory plasticity is insufficient to identify it with G1 P09's bee mushroom-body relational categorization model.
